A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable, allowing additions and removals to be distinguished from renaming, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix K report original synthetic regression simulations, GPT-2 evaluations under covariance shift, and Llama2-7B experiments on SCIQ.

after.justification: The original regression and language-model evaluations remain. Appendix L adds numerical experiments comparing temperature estimates and generalization errors under controlled distribution shifts.

M1.justification: The attention approximation, pretrained parameters, and exact optimal-temperature formula remain unchanged despite renaming. v2 adds a finite-context correction to the moment-ratio temperature heuristic in Equation (22), evaluated in Appendix L. The retained LLM experiments do not show adoption of this correction.

E1.justification: Synthetic linear regression and SCIQ remain the task coverage. The dedicated input-mean-shift experiment in v1 Appendix C/Figure 4 disappears. v2 Appendix L additionally isolates task-covariance shifts with zero task mean, alongside the retained combined task-mean/covariance experiment.

E2.justification: Removing v1 Figure 4 removes its linear-attention regression comparator. v2 Figure 6 newly compares uncorrected and corrected moment-ratio estimates against the exact optimum. The retained comparisons with unadjusted temperature and the Bayes-optimal predictor are unchanged.

E3.justification: Retained experimental settings are unchanged. New Appendix L fixes d = 50, l = 2d, and m = 5000 while varying input covariance, task covariance, or noise separately. Its noise sweep therefore uses a different context ratio from the retained l/d = 1 experiment.

E4.justification: Appendix L adds sensitivity analyses testing the moment-ratio correction and separately varying three shift parameters. These extend the existing robustness analyses. Conversely, the input-mean-shift comparison between linear and centered approximate attention in v1 Appendix C is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report 12 Monte Carlo runs and one-standard-deviation error bars for SCIQ. The added simulations introduce no new seed information, repeated-run counts, uncertainty reporting practice, or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 Figures 6-7 add temperature and generalization-error results. Figure 6b shows corrected and optimal temperatures near 1.5 versus an uncorrected estimate near 1. The mean-shift results from v1 Figure 4 disappear; retained regression, SCIQ, and GPT-2 plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: The main assumptions, generalization theorem, optimal-temperature formula, and supporting proofs are retained. v2 Sections 4.4-4.5 add an isotropic-shift specialization and a derivation connecting score moments to a finite-context correction, Equations (18)-(22), extending the earlier Appendix J heuristic.

C1.justification: The central claims remain a theoretical characterization of optimal attention temperature and improved ICL robustness under distribution shift, supported by synthetic and LLM evaluations. The revised title and abstract foreground the high-dimensional regime and moment-based guidance already present in v1.

C2.justification: New Sections 4.4-4.5 explain separate effects of input variance, task variance, noise, and context length, and argue for stronger theoretical grounding of the corrected heuristic. v1's task-diversity interpretation and explicit full-versus-partial compensation discussion are removed. Appendix J's preliminary-heuristic caveat remains.

D1.justification: v2 removes the Reproducibility Statement promising code release with the camera-ready version, without replacement release information. Appendix K retains its software, hardware, and runtime details. Appendix L documents parameter settings for the added sweeps.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and cited works largely persist, including the relocated extended discussion. However, v1 Section 4.1's explicit explanation of how its pretraining parameters generalize Von Oswald et al. (2023) is removed, modestly reducing the detailed positioning against prior theory.

P1.justification: The theoretical narrative is substantially reorganized: generalization and optimal-temperature results now precede pretraining and shift analysis, followed by dedicated interpretation sections. The title and abstract are revised, terminology changes throughout, extended related work moves from Appendix L to A, and several ancillary statements are removed.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one column to two, with extensive figure resizing and repositioning. The temperature-distribution illustration moves from v1 Appendix D/Figure 5 to v2 main-text Figure 1 with revised labels. The mean-shift figure is removed, and two new three-panel figures appear in Appendix L.

improvement.justification: v2 improves organization and adds useful heuristic diagnostics, but removes the mean-shift comparison. Its principal new derivation also has an unresolved scaling inconsistency: Equation (17) gives M11 approximately dI under isotropic training, whereas Sections 4.4-4.5 assume Tr(M11^T M11)/Tr(M11) approximately one without explaining a rescaling. This weakens confidence in the added theoretical justification. With the original main results unchanged, these benefits and harms do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
